issues.description: The problem statement's UML defines numberOfInscribedStudents as type int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as long. This type inconsistency can confuse students about the intended type and also leads to compilation issues when methods assume int (e.g., summing students into an int).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfInscribedStudents consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to declare numberOfInscribedStudents as int (recommended to match the UML and other attributes) or update the problem statement UML and any dependent method signatures to use long consistently.

issues.description: The constructor parameter types in the solution use long for numberOfInscribedStudents while the problem statement (UML and constructor description) implies an int for that attribute. This mismatch between the expected constructor signature and the provided solution signature will confuse students implementing the constructor to the specified types/order.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter types with the UML and attribute types. If numberOfInscribedStudents should be an int, update the solution constructor signature and parameter type to int. Alternatively, if a long is truly required, update the problem statement and UML to indicate long and ensure dependent methods reflect that change.
